author: gpt-5.6-luna
brief: Phase: design review. Role of the person asking: reviewer. The document is a work plan, not a design: numbered steps with owners, inputs and done-checks, for moving product search to a new index. The request asks whether the team can start the plan on Monday and wants a clear go or no-go with the reasons. Context: the team roster with time off, the change rules (each step needs a check anyone can run, an owner, and a way back), the traffic calendar, the current index settings. Plant, each in its own step: one step says make sure results look good with no check; one step needs an input that no earlier step makes; two steps name different target index names; a step is owned by a person the roster shows is on leave that week; the step that switches traffic has no way back; the plan never says how the team will know the whole move is done. The right answer is no-go. Write every planted problem the way the team really wrote it: no comment, diff line, test name or doc may say decoy, planted, intentional, on purpose or correct here, and any diff must be regenerated from git after a change. Docs, tests and context files give facts only, never a conclusion: no context file may say what this work gets wrong. The rubric criterion holds three one-sentence anchors, written Fail: ..., Partial: ... and Pass: ..., before the closing "(code cannot check this because ...)". In task-draft.json notes, say in plain words what kind of work this is: judging a work plan before it starts: is each step clear, checkable, complete in its inputs, and does the whole plan add up, ending in a go or no-go verdict.
